results.name: a safe save of a new file publishes it and leaves no temporary output
replacing an existing file advances it by one version and keeps the previous one
a save whose bytes do not match the digest the caller declared is refused, and the original is untouched
a malformed payload is refused and the file it was aimed at is untouched
text that cannot survive a byte round-trip is refused
a target that moved under the caller is refused rather than overwritten
when replacement is unavailable the bytes are published beside the original, never over it
a save whose acknowledgement was lost is answered, not performed again
a save token cannot be reused to publish different bytes
eight concurrent saves of one token publish one version
a save larger than the store limit is refused before anything is written
a temporary output abandoned by a dead process is reclaimable and age-bounded
every safe save is visible in the job journal with the stages it really went through
a safe-saved text file becomes searchable, and a refused one does not
the temporary output folder cannot be used as a target
